decisions.statement: the native shells have no lockfile of their own
An install for a native shell runs at the root of the tree above that shell.
A build on a checkout has the akasha manifest as that root.
A build on a delivered tree has a manifest written at that tree's root.
The step installing a native shell's packages installs bun first on a mac with none.
A script that never runs bun installs no bun.
the macbook keychain password is read from the MACBOOK_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD environment variable
The keychain password reaches the mac through the ssh environment.
No generated script carries the keychain password in its own text.
The password is unset before any step of the build can inherit it.
A password that did not arrive ends the run before the build lock is taken.
A ring credential is read from the NATIVE_SHELL_RING_CREDENTIAL variable.
An app whose page names no ring-credential script is asked for no credential.
A ring credential an app bakes and nothing holds ends the run before a number is spent.
Nothing forwards a ring credential to a build whose app bakes none.
the App Store Connect key id and issuer id here name one fixed Apple developer account
An app stating no widget bundle id exports no widget name and no components.
A container step running as root leaves files `git worktree remove` cannot delete.
Taking the mac checkout away falls back to `rm -rf` where `git worktree remove --force` cannot.
The script making an app's native sources is run by name rather than through a manifest.
The plugins a build compiles in are the packages the app's page reaches.

definition: the shell fragments and App Store Connect identifiers shared by every generated mac build script
